title: KiroCrew recorded walkthroughs

scenes.title: One endpoint-control boundary
scenes.description: Expand the preserved endpoint diagram, then return to the recorded ARM deployment view.
scenes.evidenceScope: Architecture reference and previously recorded deployment evidence.

cues.label: Read the reference scope
cues.detail: The diagram describes the execution boundary. Its September 11 reference label remains visible.

cues.label: Inspect the single enclosure
cues.detail: Gateway, backend, workspace and endpoint controls remain in one box.

cues.label: Move to the ARM deployment
cues.detail: The next slide describes recorded ARM deployment evidence and marks the native MCP path as pending.

scenes.title: Navigate the admin console
scenes.description: Read the remote Gateway overview, inspect the selected backend, filter its sign-in error, and open observability.
scenes.evidenceScope: Live owner-portal navigation. Native Kiro CLI authentication remains pending.

cues.label: Read the Gateway overview
cues.detail: The running Gateway reports uptime and zero completed sessions. This page shows the remote server nightly.

cues.label: Inspect the backend selection
cues.detail: Kiro CLI is selected. The GitHub card uses a separate KAS identity; the fresh CLI authentication check is false.

cues.label: Inspect the native startup failure
cues.detail: The log filter exposes the actual Kiro CLI not-logged-in error. No successful native turn is claimed.

cues.label: Open the telemetry app
cues.detail: Demo Observability combines the bounded Mac and EC2 collector samples.

scenes.title: Compare client and server telemetry
scenes.description: Refresh stored samples, expand process measurements, and filter real collection events by source.
scenes.evidenceScope: Live custom telemetry dashboard. Collection events are separate from Crew security audit events.

cues.label: Compare both sources
cues.detail: The client reports Local Gateway off while the EC2 Gateway and MCP checks are healthy. Sample times are displayed in the browser time zone.

cues.label: Refresh stored samples
cues.detail: Refresh reads the latest stored samples. The collectors run separately every 60 seconds.

cues.label: Inspect Mac process metrics
cues.detail: The expanded client measurements describe local processes and probes.

cues.label: Inspect EC2 services
cues.detail: The server detail adds Gateway and MCP main-process CPU and memory.

cues.label: Filter client events
cues.detail: Client filtering retains health changes and collection errors, including recorded historical events.

cues.label: Filter server events
cues.detail: The table now shows only server collection events.

cues.label: Return to all events
cues.detail: All restores both sources. These fixed collection labels exclude prompts and credentials.

scenes.title: Inspect native Gateway telemetry
scenes.description: Read the configured metrics switch, then inspect Gateway instruments and startup measurements.
scenes.evidenceScope: Live native Gateway instrumentation. Zero completed backend turns; separate custom collectors provide the client/server view.

cues.label: Read the telemetry settings
cues.detail: Record metrics is enabled. The environment disables anonymous reporting. This take does not change either setting.

cues.label: Inspect Gateway instruments
cues.detail: Request and process instruments contain measurements. The top summary still shows zero completed turns.

cues.label: Inspect startup measurements
cues.detail: The Startup tab displays the Gateway instrumentation already collected by this running server.

cues.label: Return to latency
cues.detail: The Latency tab restores the instruments view.

scenes.title: Follow a direct MCP request to AWS
scenes.description: Start the bounded probe, read its three outcomes, and inspect the fresh receipt.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual direct MCP/AWS execution from a standalone operator screen. Native Kiro CLI acceptance remains pending.

cues.label: Read the execution scope
cues.detail: The fixed command invokes the EC2 MCP service directly. It does not run through a native Kiro CLI turn.

cues.label: Run the bounded probe
cues.detail: The button starts the actual command. The following outcomes come from its completed result.

cues.label: Compare three outcomes
cues.detail: S3 returned the expected 55-byte object and digest. MCP rejected a disallowed tool before AWS dispatch. IAM returned AccessDenied with an AWS request ID.

cues.label: Inspect the receipt
cues.detail: The receipt records timestamps, trace IDs, the object digest and AWS request IDs. Native backend verification remains false.

cues.label: Return to the result cards
cues.detail: These outcomes establish the bounded direct probe only.

scenes.title: Rehearse the synthetic endpoint controls
scenes.description: Run the isolated control test runner, inspect the results, and open its receipt.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual execution of a local synthetic test runner. Approval is scripted; no native approval UI, backend MCP or AWS call occurs.

cues.label: Read the rehearsal scope
cues.detail: This disposable local run models endpoint controls. It does not verify native KiroCrew enforcement.

cues.label: Run the frozen control test runner
cues.detail: The button invokes the existing isolated rehearsal. The recorded wait preserves the command’s actual runtime.

cues.label: Inspect the control results
cues.detail: The test runner covers allow, scripted approval, deny, protected paths, command gating, Policy/Profile intersection and redaction.

cues.label: Read the SEL checks
cues.detail: The test runner verifies 7 of 7 entries, detects the tampered fixture at 6 of 7, then restores and verifies 7 of 7.

cues.label: Inspect the command receipt
cues.detail: The fresh receipt identifies the isolated synthetic run and keeps native backend verification false.

cues.label: Return to the rehearsal results
cues.detail: Use this scene to explain the controls while keeping native runtime acceptance pending.

reviewScope: Prior model council covers its frozen source candidate only; this derivative has no final council verdict.
